title: Tighten and fit a loose necktie
instruction: Tighten the loose necktie on the rigid plastic collar form, fit it against the collar, then release both hands. There is no person in the scene.
context: Adjusting a necktie is a familiar dressing skill and a useful form of assistance for someone with limited hand movement.
setup: A reversible woven polyester necktie, 1.26 m long, 70 mm at its wide end, 35 mm at its narrow end and approximately 1.2 mm thick, with a gold stripe. It is already threaded into a loose simple knot around a rigid plastic collar form. The knot is initially about 96 mm wide and 62 mm high, with its top 79 mm below the collar’s lower edge. The wide tip initially hangs 391 mm below that edge. The form has a 110 mm-diameter, 100 mm-high neck centred at (0.400, 0, 1.250) m, two 50 × 55 × 8 mm white plastic collar flaps and a black ink centre mark. A grey steel stand comprises a 180 × 160 × 12 mm base, 25 × 25 × 455 mm post and 210 × 25 × 25 mm support. The wooden tabletop is at z=0.7475 m. Both YAM arms start at their normal ready poses, fingers open. The screenshot and scene specify the fixed layout; the tie is not tightened or fitted.
scoring: Judge after both hands release for 5 seconds. Score 0.5 if the knot remains threaded, is at most 70 mm wide and 70 mm high, and its top is within 60 mm below the collar’s lower edge. Score 1.0 if all of the above hold and its top is within 20 mm, its centre is within 20 mm horizontally of the collar mark, the wide blade is flat within 30 degrees of untwisted, the narrow blade is behind it with its tip at least 10 mm higher, and the wide tip is 350–440 mm below the collar’s lower edge. Otherwise 0. A pulled-out end, damaged fabric or added support scores 0. Use front and rear photographs, the video and a ruler.
fidelity: Reduced model of an already-threaded tie, not full cloth physics. Idealized grasps and relative hand motion feed material through a fixed-topology wrap. Length is conserved; unsupported pulls move the tie. The knot stays in the collar’s front plane; released blades drape under a gravity approximation. Internal folds, cloth reaction forces, tearing and arbitrary rethreading are not simulated. Both policies use the same model; parameters are uncalibrated.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 in 580 steps (29 seconds). Dream-1: 0.0 in 1,200 steps (60 seconds).
reset_notes: Restore the pictured loose, already-threaded knot around the form. Reset both arms to ready with open fingers. This is a task about finishing and adjusting a prepared necktie, not tying one from an untied strip. Replace the tie if it is damaged in a physical trial.
